Title: Guest/Patient Wireless VLAN Not Isolated From Corporate LAN (Misconfigured Trunk)
Description: The access switch port serving the patient/guest WiFi SSID is configured as an 802.1Q trunk allowing tagged frames for VLAN 10 (Corporate) instead of being locked to VLAN 70 access mode.
Consequence: A patient or visitor on guest WiFi can send double-tagged 802.1Q frames to hop into the corporate VLAN, bypassing intended network segmentation entirely.
Remediation: Reconfigure guest access ports as 'switchport mode access' locked to VLAN 70 only; disable DTP negotiation; implement private VLANs and enforce 802.1x on all access ports.

Title: Windows Print Spooler Remote Code Execution (PrintNightmare)
Description: The shared print server has the Print Spooler service exposed and is missing the July 2021 out-of-band security update, making it vulnerable to PrintNightmare.
Consequence: Remote code execution as SYSTEM on the print server, enabling lateral movement across the corporate LAN and access to any host with the spooler service running.
Remediation: Apply the July 2021+ cumulative update; disable the Print Spooler service on servers that do not need it; restrict Point-and-Print to approved servers via Group Policy.

Title: Local Administrator Password Reuse Across Clinical Workstations
Description: The same local Administrator password is used across FILESRV01, nursing-station workstations, and admissions workstations, discoverable via credential dumping after initial foothold.
Consequence: Compromise of a single clinical workstation allows pass-the-hash lateral movement to all machines sharing the password, including the file server holding scheduling and HR data.
Remediation: Deploy Microsoft LAPS to randomize and rotate local admin passwords per host; audit for shared local accounts.

Title: Excessive NTFS/SMB Share Permissions - 'Everyone' Full Control on Patient Scheduling Share
Description: The \\FILESRV01\Patient-Scheduling share grants 'Everyone: Full Control' at both the share and NTFS level, rather than being restricted to the scheduling/admissions security group.
Consequence: Any authenticated (or in this case, VLAN-hopped) user can read, modify, or delete patient appointment and demographic data.
Remediation: Apply least-privilege ACLs restricting the share to the appropriate AD group; remove 'Everyone' and 'Authenticated Users' broad grants; enable share auditing.

Title: Drupal Core Remote Code Execution (Drupalgeddon2)
Description: The public patient portal runs an outdated Drupal core version vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted form API render arrays.
Consequence: An attacker can achieve full web server compromise without any credentials, enabling webshell deployment and further internal pivoting.
Remediation: Upgrade Drupal core to a patched release (>=7.58 / 8.5.1 or later, ideally migrate to a supported major version); apply a WAF rule set for known Drupalgeddon2 request patterns.

Title: Patient Portal Webshell Upload Following RCE
Description: Following exploitation of Drupalgeddon2, a PHP webshell was placed in the public files directory, which does not disable script execution.
Consequence: Persistent remote code execution on the DMZ web server, used as a pivot point into internal networks even after the original RCE is patched.
Remediation: Disable PHP execution in the public files/uploads directory via web server configuration; enforce file-integrity monitoring on the DMZ web root.

Title: Load Balancer ACL Permits DMZ-to-AppTier Traffic on All Ports (Excessive Firewall Rule)
Description: The firewall rule between the DMZ zone and the App Tier (VLAN 21) is defined as 'DMZ-net ANY -> AppTier-net ANY ALLOW' instead of restricting to the specific backend port the load balancer actually needs.
Consequence: A foothold on any DMZ host can reach any port/service on any App Tier host, drastically expanding the pivot surface into the EHR application layer.
Remediation: Rewrite the firewall policy to allow only LB01 -> EHR-APP01:7002 and equivalent explicit tuples; deny-all as default; document rule owners and review quarterly.

Title: Oracle WebLogic Server Remote Code Execution
Description: The Electronic Health Record application server runs on an unpatched Oracle WebLogic Server, vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution via a crafted console URL.
Consequence: Unauthenticated remote code execution as the WebLogic service account, enabling direct access to the EHR database connection and patient record data.
Remediation: Apply Oracle's Critical Patch Update (October 2020 CPU or later); restrict access to the WebLogic Administration Console to the management network only; place a WAF in front of the console path.

Title: EHR Application Service Account Has db_owner Rights on EHR Database (Excessive Privilege)
Description: The 'svc_ehrapp' account used by EHR-APP01 to connect to DB-EHR01 has been granted the db_owner fixed database role instead of scoped read/write on specific tables.
Consequence: RCE on the app server yields full control over the EHR database (schema changes, mass patient-record exfiltration, xp_cmdshell abuse for further OS-level pivoting).
Remediation: Recreate the service account with least-privilege GRANTs limited to required stored procedures/tables; disable xp_cmdshell; enable SQL login auditing and alerting on DDL statements from app accounts.

Title: Azure Blob Storage Container Publicly Readable - Contains SAS Token Backup File
Description: The Azure Blob Storage container 'velon-imaging-archive', intended for de-identified research images, has anonymous public read access enabled and contains an accidentally-uploaded 'app-settings-backup.json' file with a long-lived SAS token embedded in plaintext.
Consequence: Anyone on the internet can enumerate and download the container contents, harvesting a SAS token with broad read/write access to other storage resources.
Remediation: Set container public access level to Private; enable Azure Storage 'Secure transfer required' and Defender for Storage; scan repositories/configs for secrets pre-deployment; revoke and rotate the exposed SAS token immediately.

Title: Azure AD App Registration / Service Principal Has Subscription 'Owner' Role (Excessive Privilege)
Description: The service principal tied to the leaked SAS token / app settings is additionally assigned the built-in 'Owner' role at the subscription scope rather than a scoped custom role, granting unrestricted access to every resource in the subscription.
Consequence: Leaked credentials grant the attacker full administrative control of the entire Azure subscription, including the ability to create new identities, modify network security groups, and access all data stores.
Remediation: Replace with a scoped custom RBAC role following least privilege; implement Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for just-in-time elevation; enable Conditional Access requiring MFA for privileged role activation.

Title: Azure SQL Database 'velon-claims-db' Publicly Accessible With Weak Administrator Password
Description: The insurance claims database has a firewall rule allowing 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 (effectively public) and uses a weak, dictionary-guessable administrator password ('Claims2023!').
Consequence: Direct internet-facing access to the claims database combined with a crackable password allows full data exfiltration of insurance and billing records without any prior network foothold.
Remediation: Remove the open firewall rule and restrict to specific application subnets via Azure SQL firewall/VNet rules; rotate to a high-entropy password stored in Azure Key Vault with automatic rotation; enable Azure AD-only authentication.

Title: Fortinet FortiOS Authentication Bypass on Administrative Interface
Description: The clinic-to-hospital SSL-VPN concentrator runs an unpatched FortiOS build vulnerable to an authentication bypass allowing arbitrary administrative actions, including adding a new SSH key to any account.
Consequence: An attacker can add their own SSH key to an administrative account without any valid credentials, gaining full control of the VPN gateway.
Remediation: Upgrade FortiOS to a fixed release (7.0.7+/7.2.2+); audit all local accounts for unauthorized SSH keys; restrict management interface access to the management network only.

Title: VPN Split-Tunnel ACL Grants Clinic Remote Users Access to Management VLAN (Excessive Access)
Description: The VPN client policy 'Clinic-Remote-Full' routes and permits traffic to 10.20.50.0/24 (the out-of-band management VLAN), which should never be reachable from a general-purpose clinic VPN profile.
Consequence: Any compromised clinic VPN credential grants direct network reach to management infrastructure (jump hosts, hypervisor consoles, backup managers), collapsing the intended tier separation.
Remediation: Split VPN profiles by role; clinic users should only reach EHR/scheduling resources through an application-layer gateway; management VLAN should require a separate hardened PAM-brokered VPN profile with MFA.

Title: Cached Domain Admin Credentials Present on Jump Host (Credential Hygiene Violation)
Description: A domain administrator previously RDP'd into JUMP01 for troubleshooting and left cached credentials (LSASS-resident), violating the tiered administration model.
Consequence: Compromise of JUMP01 (a lower-trust bastion host) permits credential dumping and full escalation to Domain Admin.
Remediation: Implement Microsoft tiered administration (Tier 0/1/2 separation); enable Credential Guard and Protected Users group for all privileged accounts; deploy a PAM solution for just-in-time admin access.

Title: VMware vCenter Server Arbitrary File Upload Remote Code Execution
Description: vCenter Server is running a version vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file upload, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution on the underlying appliance.
Consequence: Full compromise of the virtualization management plane, granting the attacker control over every VM/ESXi host in the environment, including the EHR and imaging database servers.
Remediation: Apply VMware's patch (vCenter 6.5 U3p / 6.7 U3o / 7.0 U2c or later); restrict management-plane access to a dedicated admin subnet with no general routing; place vCenter behind an additional jump/bastion with MFA.

Title: Backup Management Console Uses Default Credentials
Description: The Veeam Backup & Replication console is still configured with the default installation service account password.
Consequence: Access to backup infrastructure allows an attacker to browse/restore backup archives (including imaging and claims data) or tamper with backup jobs to stage a ransomware event.
Remediation: Change all default credentials immediately post-install as part of the hardening checklist; integrate with AD using a dedicated least-privilege service account; restrict console access to the management VLAN with a jump-host requirement.

Title: Weak, Non-Rotated Password on Clinical Integration Service Account ('svc_clinical')
Description: The 'svc_clinical' service account (used for HL7 interface engine integration) has a weak, non-rotated password and is a member of 'Domain Users' with no additional restrictions, making it a prime Kerberoasting target.
Consequence: Any domain-authenticated user can request a TGS ticket for the SPN and crack it offline; the resulting password can potentially be reused for broader access given weak password hygiene.
Remediation: Rotate to a 25+ character randomly generated password (or migrate to a Group Managed Service Account/gMSA); enable AES-only Kerberos encryption; monitor for excessive TGS-REQ volume per account.

Title: Active Directory sAMAccountName Spoofing Privilege Escalation (noPac)
Description: DC01 is missing the November 2021 security update, leaving Active Directory vulnerable to the sAMAccountName spoofing chain that allows a standard domain user to impersonate a Domain Controller and escalate to Domain Admin.
Consequence: Near-trivial escalation from any domain user account to full Domain Admin, giving the attacker control of the entire Active Directory forest.
Remediation: Apply the November 2021 Windows Server cumulative update (or later) to all Domain Controllers immediately; monitor for anomalous machine account creation and Kerberos ticket requests (Event ID 4741/4768).

Title: Flat Trust: Clinical/Biomed VLAN Accepts Corporate AD Authentication (No Network Tiering)
Description: The firewall/ACL between the Corporate LAN (VLAN 10) and the Clinical/Biomedical critical zone (VLAN 40) permits full Active Directory authentication traffic and SMB, meaning any domain account (including a compromised Domain Admin) can authenticate directly into the highest-sensitivity zone with no additional control.
Consequence: Domain Admin compromise on the general corporate network directly cascades into the clinical device network, defeating the purpose of segmentation for life-safety-critical systems.
Remediation: Redesign as a tiered/segmented trust: the clinical zone should use a resource forest or a one-way trust with a dedicated Tier-0 admin group; firewall should allow only specific management jump-host IPs into VLAN 40, not the entire VLAN 10; require PAM/MFA step-up for any admin action inside VLAN 40.
Compliance_Ref: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e) / FDA Premarket Cybersecurity Guidance

Title: Infusion Pump Gateway - VxWorks IPnet TCP/IP Stack Buffer Overflow
Description: The infusion pump gateway workstation runs a legacy VxWorks-based real-time OS build with the vulnerable IPnet TCP/IP stack (the 'URGENT/11' vulnerability class), enabling remote buffer overflow with no authentication required from the local network segment.
Consequence: An attacker reaching the clinical device network could crash or take control of the gateway coordinating multiple bedside infusion pumps, with a plausible path to altering pump communication and posing direct patient-safety risk.
Remediation: Apply the manufacturer's firmware/software update addressing the IPnet stack per the vendor's cybersecurity bulletin; segment infusion pump gateways onto a dedicated micro-segment with no routable path from corporate AD; deploy network-based virtual patching (IDS/IPS signatures) where firmware updates require a formal change-control/clinical validation cycle.

Title: Automated Dispensing Cabinet Shares Administrative Credential With General IT Administration (Excessive Access)
Description: PHARMACY-DISPENSE01, which controls automated medication dispensing cabinets, is administered using the same Domain Admin credential set used for general corporate IT support, rather than a dedicated, isolated administrative identity.
Consequence: A Domain Admin compromise anywhere in the environment grants direct administrative access to medication dispensing controls, creating a plausible path to medication diversion or dosage tampering.
Remediation: Implement dedicated, isolated administrative identities for all clinical/pharmacy systems per FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance; require dual-control/two-person integrity for any configuration change; eliminate shared-credential administration.

Title: Spring Framework Remote Code Execution (Spring4Shell)
Description: The telehealth video-visit backend uses a bundled Spring Framework version vulnerable to a class-loader manipulation RCE exploitable via a crafted HTTP request on JDK 9+ with certain deployment configurations.
Consequence: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the application server hosting telehealth session logic.
Remediation: Upgrade Spring Framework to >=5.3.18/5.2.20; if immediate patching isn't possible, apply the interim WAF/mitigation controls Spring published (disallowedFields binder configuration); deploy egress filtering to detect anomalous outbound connections from app servers.

Title: Telehealth Service Running as Local SYSTEM Instead of Dedicated Low-Privilege Account (Excessive Privilege)
Description: The telehealth Java service is configured to run as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM instead of a dedicated, least-privilege service account, a legacy 'it just worked' configuration.
Consequence: Any code execution vulnerability in the app (such as Spring4Shell) immediately grants full SYSTEM-level control of the host rather than being contained to an application-scoped account.
Remediation: Reconfigure the Windows service to run under a dedicated 'svc_telehealth' account with only the specific rights needed; apply the principle of least privilege consistently across all application services.

Title: Hardcoded Database Credentials in Telehealth Application Configuration File
Description: The application's 'application.yml' file contains the DB-CLAIMS01 connection string with a plaintext username/password rather than referencing a secrets manager or environment-injected value.
Consequence: Local file system access (achieved via the Spring4Shell RCE) directly yields database credentials without any further exploitation needed.
Remediation: Migrate secrets to Azure Key Vault with runtime injection; rotate the exposed DB credential; add secret-scanning to the CI/CD pipeline to prevent recurrence.

Title: Excessive Database Link Privileges Between Telehealth and Claims Databases (Excessive Access)
Description: A linked-server connection from the telehealth database to the insurance claims database was created for a one-time billing-integration project and was never removed or scoped down, using a highly privileged account.
Consequence: Compromise of the telehealth application allows an attacker to pivot directly into the claims/billing database via the trusted linked-server connection without needing separate credentials, enabling insurance fraud or billing manipulation.
Remediation: Remove unused linked-server connections; where cross-database access is genuinely required, scope the linked account to specific views/procedures with read-only access rather than a trusted/passwordless link.

Title: Anonymous SMB Access Enabled on Imaging Archive NAS
Description: IMAGING-NAS01 permits anonymous/guest SMB sessions to enumerate and read the 'PACS-Archive' share.
Consequence: Sensitive diagnostic imaging archives (containing patient identifiers) can be read without any credentials by anyone who reaches the storage VLAN.
Remediation: Disable guest/anonymous SMB access; require authenticated access scoped to the Imaging-Admins group only; enable share-level auditing.

Title: Overly Permissive Firewall Rule: 'ANY-ANY-ALLOW' Left From Initial Clinic Deployment
Description: A temporary 'any-any-permit' rule created during initial outpatient clinic deployment was never removed after cutover, exposing the clinic subnet to unrestricted routing.
Consequence: Broadens the attack surface for any host on the clinic network to reach core segments beyond what business need requires.
Remediation: Perform a full firewall rule-base review; remove temporary/legacy rules; implement a formal rule lifecycle process with expiration dates and quarterly recertification.

Title: Microsoft SMBv3 Compression Remote Code Execution (SMBGhost)
Description: A clinical workstation is missing the March 2020 out-of-band update addressing a compression-handling flaw in SMBv3, enabling pre-authentication remote code execution or denial of service.
Consequence: Wormable remote code execution potential on a clinical endpoint; no active mass-exploitation confirmed at this time, but the flaw remains a high-value target given its severity.
Remediation: Apply the March 2020 out-of-band security update; disable SMBv3 compression via registry workaround where patching is delayed; restrict SMB (445/tcp) between workstations with host-based firewall rules.

Title: Azure AD: Excessive Global Administrator Role Assignments
Description: 11 user accounts hold the Global Administrator role in Azure AD, including several IT support accounts that only require Helpdesk Administrator rights.
Consequence: Any one of 11 accounts being phished grants full control of the cloud identity tenant, including the ability to reset any user's MFA and access all connected SaaS/cloud resources holding patient data.
Remediation: Apply least-privilege role assignment (use Helpdesk/User Administrator roles instead); reduce Global Admin count to <5; enable Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for just-in-time, time-bound elevation with approval workflow.

Title: Clinical/Biomedical Device Network Not Logically Isolated From General Corporate Traffic
Description: Segmentation testing shows the clinical/biomedical device network (VLAN 40) is reachable from general corporate segments through more paths than documented in the network diagram submitted for the last HIPAA risk assessment.
Consequence: Undocumented/uncontrolled pathways into the clinical device network increase both HIPAA risk-assessment scope and real-world patient-safety attack surface, and represent a potential compliance finding in the next audit cycle.
Remediation: Perform a full segmentation penetration test; update network diagrams to reflect actual traffic flows; remediate all undocumented paths and re-test before the next HIPAA Security Risk Assessment.

Title: Patient Portal Administrative Console Missing Multi-Factor Authentication
Description: The patient portal's administrative console accepts username/password authentication only, with no multi-factor authentication requirement, despite being internet-reachable.
Consequence: A leaked or brute-forced administrator credential is sufficient for full portal takeover, with no second factor to stop the attacker.
Remediation: Enforce MFA (TOTP or FIDO2/WebAuthn) for all administrative console access; add rate limiting and account lockout for repeated failed logins; monitor for impossible-travel login patterns.
